title: everything-born-of-a-test-is-flagged-and-the-shims-dispose
author: CC (Opus 5), session a187d6ab
intention: Everything a test touches — every envelope, record, trouble, and run — carries origin: test by physics, every shim disposes of flagged debris unless it declares a test handler, and the tester's runs live under the 30-day logging address, so the live system stays clean without isolating the tests from it.
how: (1) the mark: TesterDevice.run_proof sets CAIRN_TESTER_ORIGIN=<run id> in the proof process's environment (the env var convention memory); bus_client.post stamps origin: 'test' + run on every envelope when set; artifact.write stamps origin on the journal line and on records that carry a header (troubles, questions); (2) disposal: BaseShim's default receive() drops an origin:test envelope after recording it to log_path(device)/test_debris.jsonl (never the data recorder), unless the device's shim declares handles_test_mail=True; (3) contagion: a handler answering an origin:test envelope posts its reply with the same origin (shim.py:645 reply path); diagnostic.raise_trouble under the mark writes origin:test on the trouble; (4) the clear lane: trouble/shim.py:258 _fold compares envelope sender to the trouble's recipient and refuses a mismatch with a finding; (5) runs: TesterDevice writes run artifacts under address.log_path('tester')/runs/<run>/; (6) the sweep: a one-time drain of origin-less test debris (the 9 troubles, the 603 envelopes) by a scratchpad script, counts on the verdict; the 30-day sweep over ~/.cairn/logs/ stays the IOU at breadcrumb_log.py:92, named not built; (7) teeth per door under netns; measured done is the post-run census.
falsifier: DONE when (1) a proof run under the tester marks its own process (an environment mark the tester sets before the proof's process starts, read by cairn/tools/base/bus_client.py and cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py) so every envelope posted and every record written from inside it carries origin: test — physics in the two doors, not a flag a proof remembers to pass; (2) every shim's default receive() disposes of an origin:test envelope unless the device declares a test handler — one tooth per door: a fixture exchange under the mark leaves 0 undelivered envelopes and 0 recorder rows without origin:test; (3) a record born of an origin:test input inherits origin:test (a trouble raised by a test seal, a reply to a test envelope, a question opened by a test crossing) — contagion tooth over the trouble and bus doors; (4) the trouble shim's clear lane refuses a clear whose envelope sender is not the trouble's recipient (the forged clear of 2026-09-15 replays as a refusal in a tooth); (5) tester runs berth under log_path('tester')/runs/<run>/ and nothing of a run lands under ~/.cairn/devices/tester/0; (6) measured on the verdict: after one full `cairn test` over the corpus, 0 records under CairnCommons/ and 0 rows in the bus store lack origin:test yet name a /tmp or fixture path (today 9 troubles and 603 envelopes), counted by instrument before and after. RED if a proof can post or write without the mark from inside a tester run, or if a non-test envelope is disposed. WRONG INTENT if Akien wants tests isolated (a separate bus, a separate commons) — his D1 says integrate and adapt first, isolate last.
traces_to: Law 7 (a record of truth never collapses an error — a test's record must say it is a test's); Law 4 (a rule that matters is physics — the mark rides the doors, not the proof's memory); Law 6 (the clear lane honours the recipient's ownership of its trouble); memory three-retention-classes (test runs past their final result are logging, 30 days). Telos: the system is resilient to its own testing rather than isolated from it.
watchme: none, because the census instrument this ticket builds (origin-less records naming /tmp or fixture under /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/ and in the bus store) is re-run on any day by hand or by the tester's own post-run step; a probe would re-derive the census the verdict already reads.

cast_checks.collision_check: Over the whys. Bus charter (a store, not a router) — disposal is the shim's act at receive(), the bus stores the flagged envelope untouched. Tester charter (owns the seal and the run) — the tester owns the mark and the run address. Trouble device (Law 6, the recipient owns its trouble) — the sender check enforces it. cff5a197b3c4 and 87f0fc7b3514 D7 — holdings, not collisions (named in the challenge). No exclusive-and-terminal collision.
cast_checks.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs, and the ticket answers: WHAT is the mark? env CAIRN_TESTER_ORIGIN=<run id>, set in TesterDevice.run_proof's subprocess env and in cairn test's; read by os.environ.get in bus_client.post and artifact.write. WHAT does an envelope gain? origin: {'kind': 'test', 'run': <run id>} beside verb; None when unmarked. WHERE does a shim dispose? cairn/tools/base/device.py:244 default receive(): if envelope.get('origin', {}).get('kind') == 'test' and not self.handles_test_mail: append to log_path(self.device)/test_debris.jsonl, record_delivery, return None. WHAT is contagion? shim.py:645 copies envelope['origin'] onto the reply; diagnostic.raise_trouble and question.open_question read the env mark themselves (they are doors). WHERE is the sender check? trouble/shim.py:258 _fold: if gate == CLEAR_GATE and envelope['sender'] != trouble['recipient']: return a refused finding {expected: recipient, actual: sender}. WHERE do runs go? address.log_path('tester') / 'runs' / run_id. HOW is done measured? a census script counting records under CairnCommons/ and rows in the bus store that name /tmp or fixture without origin:test, run before and after one `cairn test` over the corpus; both numbers on the verdict. WHAT NOT to touch: netns isolation, the bus store schema beyond the one field, decisions/.

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: Considered isolation (a test bus, a test commons root, netns already isolates the network) — Akien's D1 rules it last resort: 'integrate and adapt first'. Considered a flag each proof passes — a proof that forgets is the hollow the doors exist to stop; the env mark set by the tester before the process starts cannot be forgotten.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: netns isolation under the tester (isolation='netns') is the isolate-last precedent already built; self-describing-fixture-names memory (transient artifacts named so they explain themselves if leaked) is the manual form of the mark; hollow-worktree-has-no-commons-beside (a proof crossing a live ticket is a live fire inside a proof) is the measured leak this makes visible. Congruency lab: the tester charter owns the seal and the run; the bus charter says the bus is a store not a router — disposal is the SHIM's act, not the bus's.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: That every path from a proof to a record passes through bus_client.post or artifact.write — a proof that writes a record with write_text bypasses both, and the artifact gate already refuses that at PreToolUse and commit; a subprocess spawned by the proof inherits the env mark. That the tester is the only test runner — `cairn test` and TesterDevice.run_proof are the two entrances and both set the mark.
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: cff5a197b3c4 (the tester takes its reply): that ticket has the tester dispose of its OWN mail; this one flags the mail at birth so every shim can dispose — distinction, not collision: cff5a197b3c4's discard_mail() becomes the tester's test handler. 87f0fc7b3514 D7 standing_raises gate (clear lane accepts any sender): the sender check here is the same fix — whichever lands first, the other reads it as a holding. Law 7: a disposed envelope is logged at the device's log home, never silently dropped.

decisions.text: Integrate and adapt, do not isolate: tests run on the live bus and live doors; resilience is built into the receivers.
decisions.by: Akien 2026-09-15 verbatim: 'my first 3 notions … were about how to ISOLATE THE PROBLEM. And I realized that's what biology does as a last resort. it'll try and integrate and adapt first.'

decisions.text: EVERYTHING born of a test is flagged origin:test — envelopes, records, troubles, replies — and only a device that declares a test handler pays attention; every other shim disposes of the debris.
decisions.by: Akien 2026-09-15 verbatim: 'if they're all flagged, then only test handlers need to pay attention. the shims otherwise dispose of the debris. same with trouble tickets. trouble tickets from testing trouble tickets even!'

decisions.text: Test runs past their final result are logging: 30-day retention, disposable.
Tester runs berth under address.log_path('tester')/runs/<run>/ (~/.cairn/logs/tester/0/runs/), never under ~/.cairn/devices/tester/0.
decisions.by: Akien 2026-09-15 verbatim: '/.cairn/devices/tester/0/runs/<run>/ i think becomes /.cairn/logging/devices/tester/0/runs/<run>/ (or whatever the logging path would be for tester, i forget) because that's where we auto-recycle-after-30-days'; address.py:148 is that path

decisions.text: The mark is physics: the tester sets CAIRN_TESTER_ORIGIN in the proof's process before it starts; bus_client.post and artifact.write stamp origin from it. A proof cannot forget the flag.
decisions.by: CC default, Akien 'i think we're in accord on that one'; Law 4; memory env-var-naming-convention

decisions.text: Contagion: a record born of a flagged input inherits the flag (reply, trouble, question).

decisions.text: The 30-day sweep over ~/.cairn/logs/ is named, not built: the IOU at breadcrumb_log.py:92 stands until a measured disk cost casts it.

There is exactly ONE place a proof process is spawned — TesterDevice.run_proof at cairn/devices/tester/device.py:506, subprocess.run(argv, env=_env_pinned_to(proof_path)) — and every entrance funnels through it (measured 2026-09-18: cairn test = cli.py:482 tester.run_proof; cairn test --hollow = hollow.py:521 tester.run_proof; the commit hook's reseal = reseal.py:384 tester.run_proof; the public door validation.py:106 TesterDevice().run_proof). So CAIRN_TESTER_ORIGIN is set in exactly one function, _env_pinned_to (device.py:188), which already builds the subject's env: env['CAIRN_TESTER_ORIGIN'] = 'test' beside the PYTHONPATH pin. No other runner exists and none is added; a proof that spawns its own subprocess inherits the env by the ordinary rules (D6 contagion). The tooth: a grep over cairn/**/*.py minus proofs/ for 'subprocess.run(' whose argv carries a proof path finds only device.py:506.

D10's literal 'test' is corrected (Law 7, later line): CAIRN_TESTER_ORIGIN carries the RUN ID — env['CAIRN_TESTER_ORIGIN'] = run_id, set in _env_pinned_to (device.py:188), run_id minted once per run_proof call as f'{utc stamp %Y%m%dT%H%M%S%f}-{pid}'. The kind is implied by the variable's existence: a reader constructs origin = {'kind': 'test', 'run': os.environ['CAIRN_TESTER_ORIGIN']} when the var is set and non-empty, else stamps nothing. The readers, by line: (a) the sole envelope builder Bus.post at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py:372 adds 'origin' to the envelope dict (the ticket's 'bus_client.post' names this door — cairn/tools/bus_client/bus_client.py has no post; every post reaches Bus.post); (b) the artifact door's journal entry builder _entry at cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py:319 adds 'origin' to the entry; (c) records with a header: DiagnosticBase.emit's record dict at cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py:287 (troubles ride raise_trouble -> emit) and open_question's record at cairn/tools/question/question.py:170 each add 'origin' the same way. One helper, cairn.tools.base.origin.test_origin() -> dict|None, is the single reader all four call.

Measured 2026-09-18: TesterDevice writes NOTHING under ~/.cairn/devices/tester/0 today (it holds bin/, groundloop/, last_known.json, tools/ — none are run artifacts), and its run artifacts are (i) the closure file, mkstemp'd in /tmp at device.py:458, and (ii) one 'run_proof' breadcrumb per run at device.py:638 that breadcrumb_log berths flat under log_path('tester') as <stamp>.TesterDevice.run_proof.json (23,548 files, no runs/ dir). The build: run_proof makes address.log_path('tester')/runs/<run_id>/ (run_id from D11) and writes the closure file there as closure.json plus the returned record as run.json; the breadcrumb keeps its address (breadcrumb_log owns it, Law 6) and carries values={'run': run_id}. No migration of the 23,548 standing breadcrumbs — they are logging under D3 and age out.

Contagion is one reader, four sites, no handler logic: test_origin() (D11) is read at Bus.post (a reply posted from inside a marked process carries it — the shim.py:645 reply path needs no change because it posts through Bus.post), at DiagnosticBase.emit (so raise_trouble's emission carries it), at open_question (question.py:170), and at artifact._entry. A record born OUTSIDE a marked process from a marked input — a shim handling an origin:test envelope in an unmarked device process — copies the envelope's origin onto its reply at the one reply path shim.py:645 (the reply carries reply_to; the origin rides beside it). Those are the only two mechanisms: env at birth, copy at reply.

The census is a module, not a scratchpad script: cairn/devices/tester/debris_census.py, run as PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.debris_census, printing one JSON line {'commons': n, 'bus': n, 'at': <utc>} where commons = count of records under CairnCommons/troubles, questions, tickets whose text names /tmp or a fixture path (regex (/tmp/|fixture)) and carry no origin field, and bus = the same count over the bus store's envelope table (why/body text) via db_domain. It is invoked by hand, twice — before the drain and after one full 'cairn test' — and its two lines are pasted verbatim as the verdict's evidence; the verdict's instrument is that one command. D8's numbers (9 troubles, 603 envelopes) are the first 'before' it must reproduce.
decisions.step: unlisted: Build the census instrument to measure before/after test debris counts

decisions.text: handles_test_mail is a class attribute on BaseShim (cairn/tools/base/shim.py:223), default False, read in BaseShim.deliver (shim.py:750) before the handler dispatch: an envelope carrying origin.kind == 'test' on a shim whose class leaves it False is appended to log_path(<device>)/test_debris.jsonl and dropped (no bounce, no handler). A device that must answer test mail sets handles_test_mail = True in its own shim's class body — that is the whole declaration, no registry. Measured 2026-09-18: grep handles_test_mail over cairn/ is 0 hits today, so every shim starts disposing; which shims must declare True is MEASURED at build, not guessed: run one full cairn test under the mark, then for each device whose test_debris.jsonl gained an envelope that a proof waited on (the proof reds or times out on a missing reply), set True in that shim and re-run; the resulting list and count ride the verdict.

D5 as built: CAIRN_TESTER_ORIGIN='<run_id>' with run_id = f'{utc now:%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%f}-{os.getpid()}' minted once per TesterDevice.run_proof call and set in _env_pinned_to (D11 carries the reader sites).

D6 as built: one helper cairn.tools.base.origin.test_origin() -> {'kind':'test','run':<id>} | None, called at exactly four record-building doors — Bus.post (bus.py:372), DiagnosticBase.emit (diagnostic.py:287), open_question (question.py:170), artifact._entry (artifact.py:319) — plus the copy at the shim reply path shim.py:645 (D13).
D8 as built: the before/after census is python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.debris_census (D14), run by hand twice, its two JSON lines the verdict's evidence — not a scratchpad script.

Pre-listed by measurement 2026-09-18 (grep bus.request/bus.post with a real device as 'to' over cairn/**/proofs): the shims whose verbs proofs drive over a bus are inference_domain (test_resolve_verb.py, test_bus_infer.py, test_inference_rides_the_bus.py), codemother (test_codemother.py, test_charter_held.py), charter (test_charter_held.py) and trouble (test_trouble.py clear/reconcile lanes) — these four declare handles_test_mail = True at build; every other 'to' in proofs is a fixture name (b, bob, poke_c, echo_a ...) served by fixture shims defined inside the proof, which inherit BaseShim's False and are handed the flag by the proof that defines them if the proof expects a reply. The correlation, should a fifth appear: a proof waiting on a disposed reply reds by timeout on its request(); the disposed envelope's id is the last line of log_path(<device>)/test_debris.jsonl for the addressee; the id in the proof's stderr and the id in the debris line match, which names the shim. Both the pre-list and any addition ride the verdict.

One proof, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_everything_born_of_a_test_is_flagged.py, PROVES = {'71d1bbfa98b0': {'1'..'6'}}, run by the tester under netns like every proof: (1) test_the_mark_is_set_in_the_subject_env — run_proof over a fixture proof that prints os.environ['CAIRN_TESTER_ORIGIN']; the printed value matches the run id on the returned record; (2) test_an_envelope_born_under_the_mark_carries_origin — with the env set in-process, a fresh Bus().post(...) returns an envelope whose origin == {'kind':'test','run': id}; with it unset, no origin key; (3) test_a_journal_line_and_a_question_and_an_emission_carry_origin — artifact.write to a scratch record, open_question(root=scratch) and DiagnosticBase.emit under the mark each carry origin; (4) test_a_shim_that_does_not_handle_test_mail_disposes — a fixture BaseShim subclass with the default False receives an origin:test envelope via deliver(): its handler is never called, log_path(device)/test_debris.jsonl (roots pointed at scratch) gains the line, no bounce; a subclass with True gets the handler call; (5) test_a_reply_and_a_trouble_inherit_the_flag — the True shim's handler replies through the reply path and raises a trouble; both carry the same origin; (6) test_the_clear_lane_refuses_a_forged_sender — the replayed 2026-09-15 21:44 clear (sender != recipient) through trouble/shim.py:258 _fold returns the finding and the trouble's count is unchanged. The run-address tooth is (1) extended: runs/<id>/run.json and closure.json exist under a scratch log root. Fixture roots override via the existing roots= parameters (address.log_path(roots=...), Bus(...) in-memory) — no live store is touched.
decisions.step: unlisted: Write one proof tooth per door (bus_client, artifact, device receive, trouble clear lane, tester run address) to verify that origin marking propagates and disposal works under netns

why: A proof's mail and troubles land beside a hand's with nothing to tell them apart, so the live inbox, the trouble list, and the bus fill with debris that a hand must sweep — and a lane that cannot tell a test from a hand cannot tell a forgery from an owner either.
depends_on: skills tier (implementation-order-claude-first); cff5a197b3c4 preferred first (the tester's own discard becomes its test handler). Tier 3.

measured_at_cast.census: measured 2026-09-16: 9 of 233 records under CairnCommons/troubles/ name a /tmp or fixture path (e.g. seal-red-cairn-tools-proof-coverage.json, workflow-cursor-unreadable-by-the-chokepoint.json); the bus held 677 undelivered envelopes on 2026-09-15 of which 603 were codemother->tester sealed replies about /tmp fixture proofs (628 on 2026-09-16); ~/.cairn/logs/tester/0/ holds 21,876 emission files back to 2026-08-22 and no runs/ directory exists under ~/.cairn/devices/tester/0 (bin, groundloop, last_known.json, tools); cairn/tools/base/address.py:148 log_path(device, instance) is the logging address (ruled 2026-08-18); cairn/tools/base/breadcrumb_log.py:92 'No rotation and no ~30-day evaporation' is the standing IOU; cairn/devices/trouble/shim.py:258 _fold clears a trouble with by=values.get('by') or 'cc' and never compares the envelope sender to the trouble's recipient — on 2026-09-15 21:44 a forged clear_trouble from a non-recipient was folded and cleared the standing red seal-red-cairn-tools-tree; no origin field exists on a bus envelope (keys id, sender, addressee, channel, kind, why, body, reply_to, date, verb) or on an artifact-door journal line.
